finalText:
All 4 tests pass now.

**Root cause:** `src/jobs/processOrder.js` called `pool.acquire()` and only `pool.release(conn)` on the happy path — if `run()` rejected (bad order payload), the connection was never returned to the pool. Every failed order permanently shrank the pool by one connection (the pool has no timeout-based reclaim by design). The logs confirm this exact progression: sporadic `invalid order payload` errors starting ~01:56 → `pool exhausted` errors on the worker by 02:06 → cascading `acquire timeout`/503s across api, worker, and scheduler by 02:11, which is your 2am page.

`src/handlers/api.js` was already safe — it goes through `withConnection`'s try/finally.

**Fix:** wrapped the `run()` call in `processOrder` with try/finally so `pool.release(conn)` always runs, mirroring the existing safe pattern. Tests are green.
